name: Personal insurance policies and claims
one_line: An individual's or household's own insurance situation on the Finance schema: the carrier that issued a policy, what the policy covers, and the documents a policy and a claim generate over their life - declarations pages, ID cards, endorsements, premium notices, adjuster estimates, settlement letters. Recommended institution, then record_type; account_type is an optional level, not a default one. A safety situation: local-only extraction, protection before any cloud or placement path.

deterministic: the declarations-page structure, as a PAIR of labelled slots on one document: a labelled policy-period slot (an effective date together with an expiration date) co-occurring with a labelled coverage, limit or deductible slot. 00 makes the labelled slot the direct-fact source - "Deterministic extractors create direct facts when the information comes from a reliable, explicit source, such as a content hash, EXIF timestamp, a document title, or a labeled form field" - and names the location this material uses: "Tables matter because resumes, forms, applications, invoices, and administrative documents often place their most useful information in cells rather than body paragraphs." The pair is the discriminator: a marketing quote carries coverage language and no policy period, a premium notice carries a period and no coverage table.

a labelled policy-number slot together with an organization-gazetteer hit matched at word boundary in the letterhead or page-one heading zone. 00: "It should use word-boundary matching rather than substring matching", and "It should use positional weighting because a value in a filename or document title carries more meaning than the same value in a footer or a late body-page reference." The gazetteer's contents are R4's and the term patterns are R6's; this row names the rule family and writes neither a list nor a regex.

an account_type source that is a labelled coverage-line or policy-type slot on the record itself - never the carrier's name and never product marketing elsewhere on the page. One carrier writes several lines for the same household, which is the whole reason the coverage line is a separate fact from the carrier.

the claim structure, as a labelled claim-number slot co-occurring with a labelled date-of-loss (or date-of-service) slot and a labelled estimate, settlement or payment total. This is what separates claim material from policy material inside the same situation, and it is the anchor a claim group is built from.

the ID-card structure in OCR or in a small text document: an organization-gazetteer hit at word boundary beside a labelled policy or member number and a labelled effective-date range, on a card-shaped capture. The OCR content is the evidence, never the image's format or the absence of camera metadata.

an email whose labelled sender slot resolves to a carrier at word boundary and whose labelled subject slot carries a premium, renewal or policy term, with an amount in a labelled body position. 00's email extractor yields "sender, recipients, subject, sent date, thread identifiers, message body, attachment names, and reply-chain context, while treating addresses and message content as potentially sensitive"; source_type alone is never sufficient (see never_alone).

an archive whose manifest lists declarations-shaped, ID-card-shaped or claim-shaped member names, read without unpacking - 00: "Archives should be inspected without being unpacked to disk." The manifest is the evidence; the outer archive name is not.

the personal-versus-commercial discriminator, stated as a rule family rather than a person detector: an organization-gazetteer hit filling the labelled named-insured slot pushes the file to the corporate sibling; a labelled named-insured slot with no organization hit, beside a labelled residential mailing address, is this situation. Where the named insured is a sole proprietor the rule cannot decide and the file goes to needs_llm rather than to a guess.
needs_llm: an unlabelled prose letter from a carrier whose subject is a policy action - a premium increase, a non-renewal, a cancellation, a coverage change - with no labelled period, coverage or claim slot anywhere. 00 lists "unlabeled forms" among the reasons rules alone are insufficient, and scopes the call: "an LLM receives only compact evidence packets for files or groups that remain ambiguous, have multiple plausible domains, or contain language that requires interpretation."

deciding whether a policy is a household's or a business's when the named insured is a sole proprietor, a landlord operating personally, or a person whose own name is the business name - the case the deterministic discriminator above cannot settle, and exactly 00's multiple-plausible-domains eligibility.

an OCR'd screenshot from a carrier app: deciding whether it shows an ID card, a claim status page, a quote comparison, or a marketing page. 00 names the ambiguity for exactly this kind of file - a PNG "may be a screenshot of a receipt, application portal, conversation, code error, or research figure".

whether a heterogeneous set of files is purpose-coherent as ONE claim - loss photographs, an adjuster estimate, a rental-car receipt, a repair invoice, a settlement letter - answered from a dossier with citations. "A model that cannot cite sufficient evidence must return unknown."

whether loss photographs belong to a claim at all, when they carry capture metadata and no readable text. 00 requires the abstention to be available: "The model must be allowed to conclude that no meaningful association exists."

a multilingual or non-domestic carrier's policy whose document-kind term has no gazetteer entry and whose slots are unlabelled; 00 names "multilingual documents" among the cases fixed patterns cannot capture.

separating this situation from its siblings when the structure is genuinely shared - a health plan's summary of benefits, a commercial certificate of insurance and a personal declarations page all carry a carrier, a policy number and a period, and only the named insured and the coverage rows say which situation it is.
never_alone: the word "policy" alone, in a filename, heading or body. This is the tempting-false-file rule for this node: a website privacy policy, an employer's HR policy handbook, a returns policy, a refund policy and a policy paper all carry it, and a downloads folder is full of them. The term needs a labelled policy-number, policy-period or coverage slot beside it to mean an insurance contract.

a carrier or organization name alone. A comparison-shopping quote, a marketing mailer, an employer's benefits brochure and a news PDF each carry one. 00's ambiguity sentence is the reason - "Columbia can appear as an authoring school, course provider, target institution, employer, research venue, or merely a cited organization" - and an insurer is one more reading of the same string.

a digit string read as a policy number. It is equally an order number, an invoice id, a case number, a member id, a claim number or a device serial; it needs a labelled policy slot or a policy-term context to mean anything.

a money figure alone. A premium, a deductible, a coverage limit, a settlement, a repair quote and a compensation figure are indistinguishable as figures; the labelled slot they sit in is the evidence, never the number.

a bare 4-digit token read as tax_year, whether it comes from the filename, the policy period or an effective-date range. 00: documents contain "numbers that look like years but are course identifiers, version numbers, build numbers, ZIP codes, or other unrelated values", and "Date candidates should be identified with explicit regular expressions and then parsed without fuzzy matching." A policy period covering part of a year is not a record of that tax year.

a source_type of email, image, ocr, archive or opaque_binary alone. 00: the engine should "treat the file extension as a routing signal rather than an assumption about meaning" - an email is not a premium notice, a .zip is not a policy packet, a photograph is not a claim.

camera EXIF on a photograph of a damaged car, roof or room, read as claim evidence. A dented bumper is a photograph of a dented bumper; only a claim group accepted on its own anchors makes it claim material, and 00 forbids the reverse reading too - "the system must not mistake the absence of EXIF for proof that an image is a screenshot", with "conflicting signals should lead to abstention rather than an invented classification".

membership in a download session that bundled several PDFs from a carrier portal. 00: "A session should never be treated as proof of topic" - it is a purpose clue and a review aid, and here it is exactly the clue that would wrongly absorb an unreadable export into a policy group.

a carrier-shaped filename stem on a file whose content cannot be read. 00 says the system "should not infer a purpose from their filename alone" for unreadable, encrypted, corrupted or unsupported files.

a residential address or a vehicle identifier alone. A homeowners declarations page, a deed, a utility bill, a vehicle service record and a registration all carry them; the sibling household-property and vehicle-records situations are reached by the same tokens, and the coverage-and-period structure is what separates them.

work_types: full policy contract or coverage booklet
grouping_reasons: one policy at one carrier across its lifecycle - the declarations page, its endorsements, each renewal's replacement declarations, the ID cards and the premium notices. The anchor is the stable labelled policy-number slot, never the carrier name alone, which 00's generic-hub rule forbids as a sole bridge

one claim across its documents - the first-report acknowledgment, the adjuster estimate, the repair or rental receipts, the settlement letter - anchored by a labelled claim number and a labelled date of loss
loss photographs attached to that claim group as context-supported members, with no insurance fact written onto them. 00: "The graph does not automatically copy those missing facts onto sparse files"
one policy re-issued: last cycle's declarations and this cycle's replacement, which is the universal version_family fact, and a re-downloaded copy, which is duplicate_family - never a finance fact

a policy document that also supports another purpose - a certificate of insurance inside a lease packet, a declarations page inside a mortgage closing packet, a premium receipt inside a tax-year packet. 00: "A file may validly belong to more than one accepted group" - multi-membership, never a copied fact

template.why: institution first, because a record_type value such as "declarations page" or "claim estimate" is unintelligible without knowing which carrier issued it - 00's parent-dimension rule, stated for coursework and general in form: "A work type such as Homework 3 is meaningful only after the course is known, and a course code may require the school or term to disambiguate it." record_type as the leaf, because the documents a household actually needs to find again are separated by kind: the card it shows at a roadside, the declarations page a lender asks for, the estimate a claim turns on. account_type - the coverage line, auto or homeowners or renters or life - is deliberately NOT a default level and IS the optional branch pattern 00's template definition provides for ("Each template should define the domain’s allowed fact fields, detection signals, recommended folder dimensions, preferred dimension order, optional branch patterns, privacy rules, and validation constraints"). The reason it is optional rather than default: most households hold one line per carrier, so a coverage-line level under each carrier would usually open a branch with a single child, and 00 warns against exactly that - "It should warn when a level produces only one child, repeats a concept already expressed in the parent, creates excessive depth, or creates a large number of tiny folders" and "It should recommend flattening when a dimension does not materially improve retrieval." Where one carrier does write several lines for the same household (auto plus home plus umbrella bundled), account_type is inserted between institution and record_type, which is 00's own instruction that "each branch should offer the dimensions that are actually present in its member groups". tax_year is destination_eligible on the canonical row and is excluded here: a policy period is not a tax year, 00's narrow-date rule forbids deriving one from an effective-date range, and the tax-year use of insurance records (premium deductibility) belongs to the corporate sibling, not to a household. The general rule points the same way - "For document and record domains, project, function, or subject usually comes before time because putting year first scatters related work across calendar folders." account_holder, the finance schema row's proposed search-and-privacy key, is never a dimension: "It should avoid using authorship or creator identity as a destination dimension." Safety posture: shallow by intent, a recommendation over a protected area rather than a filing tree - "a Finance or Identity proposal may be visible as a protected area, but the product should avoid showing sensitive filenames or sending their contents to cloud services by default." And all of it is reversible by the user: "The system recommends an order based on the domain template, but the user can reverse, remove, add, or flatten dimensions." Whether a household is better served by carrier-first or coverage-line-first is recorded in open_question rather than decided here.

observations: page-one letterhead carries an organization name matched at word boundary
labelled slots: Named Insured, Policy Number, Policy Period with an effective and an expiration date
a labelled header cell reads Personal Auto Policy
a coverage table with labelled limit and deductible columns, and a labelled Total Premium
a vehicle block listing year, make, model and a vehicle identification number
a footer names a local agency, distinct from the letterhead carrier
must_not_conclude: tax_year from the policy period or from the filename's 4-digit token - a policy period is not a tax year, and a bare 4-digit run is 00's forbidden year candidate

institution = the agency named in the footer rather than the carrier in the letterhead; 00 ranks the letterhead position above a footer occurrence, and an agency is a distributor rather than the issuer
a vehicle or address fact - the schema declares no such field, and the identification number is protected identifier material that must not surface in a summary or a model prompt
a folder path

observations: carrier name in the page-one letterhead
labelled Named Insured slot holding an individual's name
labelled Certificate Holder slot holding a property-management company
labelled Policy Number and a labelled effective-and-expiration date pair
a liability limit row and a personal-property limit row
must_not_conclude: institution = the certificate holder. The property manager is the party the document is addressed TO; the carrier is the party that issued it. 00: "The system must separate roles that happen to contain the same entity type", and for this domain, "A finance document may mention an account holder and an issuing bank" - the same split, with a carrier in the issuer role
a lease fact, a landlord fact or a tenancy term - none of those is a field this schema declares, and the lease itself is a different file
that the certificate holder being an organization makes this the corporate situation; the NAMED INSURED is what discriminates, and here it is an individual
a folder path

observations: camera EXIF present: make, model, DateTimeOriginal, GPS
sensor-shaped pixel dimensions
OCR of the frame returns no usable text - the subject is hail damage to a roof
arrived in the same folder as an adjuster estimate
must_not_conclude: ANY insurance fact from this file. It carries no carrier, no policy number, no claim number and no readable text; the insurance reading comes entirely from the neighbourhood, and 00 forbids importing it - "The graph does not automatically copy those missing facts onto sparse files"
institution or record_type from the folder it sits in or from the download session that produced it
an event fact from the GPS alone - a location is not an occasion
a folder path

observations: carrier name in the page-one letterhead
labelled slots: Claim Number, Date of Loss, Insured, Adjuster, Policy Number
a line-item repair table with labelled quantity, unit and extended-cost columns
a labelled Net Claim total and a labelled Deductible line
a repair vendor's name appears in several table rows
must_not_conclude: a claim-number field. The claim number is evidence and a grouping anchor, not a schema field - minting one would be a private key on the shared vocabulary, and 00 is explicit that the system "should not invent new fields automatically"
institution = the repair vendor read out of the estimate rows; a vendor inside a table is not the record's issuer
tax_year from the date of loss
a folder path

observations: PNG at an exact display resolution; no camera EXIF
filename carries the platform's default screenshot pattern
an OCR region reads a carrier name beside a labelled Policy Number, an ID Card heading, and a labelled effective-date range
a second OCR region reads a vehicle description
must_not_conclude: media_type = screenshot from the missing EXIF alone; the exact display resolution and the filename pattern are what may support it, and "conflicting signals should lead to abstention rather than an invented classification"
that this file carries the policy group's facts because it names the same carrier - it may join the policy neighbourhood as a context-supported member without inheriting anything
a folder path, and no cloud dossier: the frame shows a policy number in the clear

observations: labelled sender slot resolves to a carrier domain at word boundary
labelled subject slot carries a premium term and a policy-shaped identifier
body carries a labelled Amount Due, a labelled Due Date and an autopay notice
one attachment named for a billing statement
no labelled coverage table anywhere
must_not_conclude: activation from source_type = email; the labelled sender and subject slots are what fire, and a source_type is never alone
account_type from the carrier's product marketing in the footer - a labelled coverage-line slot on the record is the only source
a contact fact used as a folder proposal; 00 keeps address-book data privacy-protected rather than a proposal basis
a folder path

observations: letterhead organization name matched at word boundary
body is prose paragraphs explaining a rate change effective on a stated date
no labelled period, coverage, claim or policy-type slot anywhere
a policy-shaped identifier appears once inside a paragraph
DOCX author metadata names a document-generation tool
must_not_conclude: account_type - no labelled coverage-line slot exists, and a coverage word inside prose is not a labelled slot
a policy fact from the mid-paragraph identifier alone
institution from the DOCX author or producer metadata rather than the letterhead; 00 treats producer strings as supporting evidence only
a folder path

observations: manifest lists declarations-shaped members for two carriers, an ID-card image, an adjuster estimate, and a scanned driving licence
manifest read without extraction to disk; member count and uncompressed size recorded
outer archive name carries no carrier, policy or year token
must_not_conclude: member facts written onto the archive, or the archive's facts written onto members - the manifest is evidence of a candidate packet for review
one institution for the archive because two carriers appear in the manifest; ranking one because it appears more often is the polished-but-false move
that the licence scan is insurance material because it arrived in this archive - it activates identity on its own evidence and is protected there
a folder path

observations: named parties: a carrier and a claimant, in a recitals block
numbered clauses including a release of further liability
a labelled Claim Number and a labelled settlement amount
an execution block with signature and date lines and a notary line
must_not_conclude: that finance activating excludes legal, or the reverse. Both read this file on disjoint evidence - the carrier-and-claim structure on one side, the parties, recitals, numbered clauses and execution block on the other - and legal is a field-less safety placeholder today, so its activation carries protection rather than fields
a settlement figure as a fact; an amount is content, not a schema field, and this is protected material
tax_year from the execution date
a folder path, and no cloud dossier

file_examples.filename: Certificate of Insurance - ABC Contracting LLC.pdf
observations: carrier name in the page-one letterhead
labelled Named Insured slot resolving to an organization at word boundary in the organizations gazetteer
labelled Certificate Holder slot naming a client company
coverage rows labelled General Liability, Automobile Liability and Workers Compensation, with per-occurrence and aggregate limits
labelled policy numbers and an effective-and-expiration date pair
must_not_conclude: that this is the personal situation. It is the collision fixture: the carrier name, the policy number and the coverage-and-period pair fire for both siblings, and the discriminating evidence is that the named insured resolves to an organization and the coverage lines are commercial. One evidence item must count for one side only - here it is finance.insurance-corporate
account_type from the commercial coverage rows as though they were a household coverage line
a folder path

observations: insurer name in the page-one letterhead
labelled slots: Claim Number, Date of Service, Provider, Amount Billed, Plan Paid, Patient Responsibility
a coded procedure column in a table
a labelled Member ID rather than a policy-and-vehicle or policy-and-property block
must_not_conclude: that this is the personal-insurance situation. The claim number and the carrier name fire for both, and the discriminating evidence is the provider, date-of-service and coded-procedure structure with a member id - that is the finance.insurance-healthcare sibling, and the medical safety placeholder co-activates on the clinical content at schema level
an account_type from the plan name unless a labelled plan or coverage slot supports it
a folder path, and no cloud dossier: this is protected material

observations: the PDF is password-protected: no text layer is reachable and no metadata beyond the filesystem record
the filename carries a policy-shaped word and nothing else
arrived in the same download session as two readable declarations pages
must_not_conclude: institution, account_type or record_type from the filename - 00: the system "should not infer a purpose from their filename alone" for unreadable files, and "policy" is this node's most ambiguous word
membership in the policy group because the download session bundled it; a session is a possible-grade clue only
a folder path

collides_with.signal: both carry a carrier in the letterhead, a labelled policy number and a labelled coverage-and-period pair - identical structure, slot for slot. The discriminating evidence is the labelled NAMED INSURED slot: an organization-gazetteer hit at word boundary is the corporate situation; an individual's name beside a residential mailing address is this one. A commercial certificate's client company in the certificate-holder slot must not be read as the discriminator. Fixture: Certificate of Insurance - ABC Contracting LLC.pdf. Where the named insured is a sole proprietor neither side may take the evidence item and the file goes to the LLM step.

both carry a carrier, a claim number and a member or policy identifier. The discriminating evidence: a provider, date-of-service and coded-procedure structure with a member id is the healthcare situation; a policy-period-plus-coverage-limit structure attached to a vehicle, a dwelling or a life is this one. The carrier name and the claim number are the two items that must never count for both. Fixture: Explanation of Benefits.pdf.

a premium invoice and an ordinary receipt both carry an organization and a labelled amount. The discriminating evidence: a labelled policy identifier with a coverage or renewal term is a premium notice; a labelled single total with an order or purchase term and no policy is a receipt. Fixture: Premium Invoice Feb 2026.eml, which sits on the seam and falls through to Receipts and Confirmations when no policy group is accepted.

an auto policy and a vehicle service record carry the same vehicle description and identification number. The discriminating evidence: labelled coverage limits, a deductible and a policy period issued by a carrier is this situation; a labelled odometer reading, service or repair-order structure from a garage or dealer is the vehicle-records situation. The vehicle identifier is the item that must not count for both.

a homeowners or renters declarations page and a property record carry the same residential address. The discriminating evidence: labelled dwelling and personal-property limits with a policy period is this situation; a deed, title, appraisal or closing structure is the property situation. The address is the item that must not count for both.

a lender requires and often escrows a homeowners policy, so a closing packet and a servicing statement both carry a carrier name and a policy number. The discriminating evidence: a labelled principal, interest and escrow breakdown with a loan number is the loans situation; a labelled coverage-and-period pair issued BY the carrier is this one. A declarations page inside a closing packet is a legitimate multi-membership, not a merge.

a liability claim and a legal matter share parties, a loss event and a money figure. The discriminating evidence: an insurer's claim-number, date-of-loss and estimate structure is this situation; a court caption, docket number, or parties-recitals-numbered-clauses drafting is the matter. Fixture: Settlement and Release.pdf, which genuinely reads as both at schema level and is why the item-level rule matters - the claim number must count once.

a personal-injury auto or liability claim file legitimately contains provider bills and treatment summaries. The discriminating evidence: an insurer's claim and settlement structure is this situation; a clinical record with a provider, an encounter and findings is the health-records situation. The patient name and the date of service are the items that must not count for both, and both readings are protected, so a wrong call does not leak - it misfiles.

loss photographs and ordinary photographs are indistinguishable by capture metadata: both carry camera EXIF, a capture time and often GPS. There is no discriminating evidence on the file itself - the claim reading exists only in an accepted claim group, and 00 forbids reading the metadata either way as proof. The correct outcome for the file alone is photos facts and no insurance facts. Fixture: IMG_7742.HEIC.

a screenshot of a carrier app and any other screenshot share the absence of camera EXIF, an exact display resolution and the platform filename pattern. The discriminating evidence is only the OCR content: a carrier beside a labelled policy number and an effective-date range is an insurance record; capture properties with no such structure are a capture only. Fixture: Screenshot 2026-02-19 at 14.03.02.png.

falls_through_to.why: 00 names this situation's material in the definition itself: "sensitive isolated material such as passport scans, medical documents, account statements, visas, legal forms, or credentials", and the residual carries its own restriction - "it should normally remain local-only and must not cause filenames or content to be exposed in model prompts". Fixtures: Auto Policy Declarations 2026.pdf, Claim 0834562 - Adjuster Estimate.pdf and Settlement and Release.pdf where no policy or claim group is accepted.

00's definition fits the one-off policy document with a durable purpose and no series: "standalone certificates, notices, confirmations, forms, and PDFs that have a durable purpose but no broader group". Fixtures: Renters Certificate of Insurance.pdf, Notice of Premium Increase.docx.

00 defines it for "isolated invoices, delivery confirmations, booking records, boarding passes, purchase receipts, event tickets, and similar transactional documents" - the isolated premium notice with no accepted policy group is exactly that. Fixture: Premium Invoice Feb 2026.eml.

00 defines it for "screenshots that appear time-sensitive or remind the user of something but have no accepted project, trip, application, or event relationship" - the ID card captured before a drive, when no policy group is accepted. Fixture: Screenshot 2026-02-19 at 14.03.02.png.

00 defines it for "images with no event, project, reference collection, or photo-family association" - the correct home for loss photographs when no claim group is accepted, and the honest alternative to inventing a claim association for them. 00's parallel warning is explicit: the model "must not invent a folder called Travel/Flight Gate B12 or assume that a gate number identifies a particular trip". Fixture: IMG_7742.HEIC.

00 defines it for "password-protected archives, unreadable documents, damaged files, and unknown formats", and carriers routinely deliver policy packets as password-protected PDFs. Fixture: Policy Documents.pdf.

sensitivity_why: 00 names this material inside its privacy sentence - the corpus "can include identity documents, account statements, tax records, medical information, legal records, credentials, private correspondence, GPS metadata, employment materials, and educational records" - and requires immediate protection for the record kinds this situation produces: "A scanned passport, tax statement, medical document, authentication key, or account record should enter a protected state immediately." "Protected material should not be included in cloud-model prompts by default", and the canvas shows it as a protected area: "a Finance or Identity proposal may be visible as a protected area, but the product should avoid showing sensitive filenames or sending their contents to cloud services by default." Only 00's phrase is asserted; the handling class is P7's and is not set here. Two cases in this situation are sharper than the schema row's general posture and are the reason its privacy rules differ from the finance default: a personal declarations page concentrates a home address, a vehicle identification number and often a driving-licence number on one page, and a personal-injury claim file carries treatment detail that 00 puts in the same protection sentence as a medical document. Loss photographs carry GPS, which 00 also names in the privacy sentence, so a claim group's members are not uniformly safe merely because the estimate is redacted.
open_question: Should a household's personal insurance branch be carrier-first or coverage-line-first? This row recommends institution then record_type, which follows 00's parent-dimension rule and matches CONNECTION-EXAMPLES fixture 8, and it offers account_type as an optional level between them. The competing design is real and is how many households actually think: the coverage line (auto, home, renters, life) is the durable thing and the carrier is what changes when a person shops around, so Auto/2026-Carrier/ retrieves better than Carrier/Auto/ for someone who has switched insurers twice. Choosing between them decides a real filing shape for someone's records and depends on whether their carriers are stable, which no evidence in a file can say. Recorded, not resolved: no field was proposed and no second dimension order was frozen, because widening account_type into the default level to make the familiar shape expressible is the move that must be Joseph's rather than a template row's. Two smaller items ride on the same answer and are recorded here rather than minted: the certificate-holder role on a certificate of insurance has no canonical counterpart key to split against, and the policy period has no canonical field at all - it must not be taken as tax_year, and the sibling finance.personal-records already carries the general year-level question.
